pages.text: Jurassic period information and facts | National Geographic SCIENCE What is the Jurassic period and why did it end? The heyday of dinosaurs, the Jurassic era saw Earth’s climate change from hot and dry to humid and subtropical. The Jurassic period was characterized by a warm, wet climate that gave rise to lush vegetation and abundant life. Many new dinosaurs emerged—in great numbers. Above, Dimorphodon reptiles fly over a herd of Mamenchisaurus dinosaurs coming down to a river for a drink. Illustration by CoreyFord, Getty Images By National Geographic Staff Last updated August 18, 2025 The Jurassic is a geologic period that took place about 201.3 million years to 145 million years ago and constitutes the middle part of the Mesozoic era . The Jurassic period was named after the Jura limestone deposits in the Jura Mountains, discovered by German geologist Alexander von Humboldt . Building on this find, French scientist Alexandre Brongniart later coined the Jurassic period. There are three Jurassic time periods: early, middle, and late. Overall, the Jurassic gives us a particularly well-preserved fossil record of prehistoric life, which included theropod dinosaurs that scientists believe evolved to become birds . Thanks to this rich record, we know that the Jurassic was the age of dinosaurs roaming a tropical Earth filled with ferns, flowering plants, and conifers. It was also a time when sea monsters, sharks, and blood-red plankton filled inland seas borne of crumbling landmasses. Here’s what the Jurassic period was really like. Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn K2-Play Completes Final Phase of North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan Oct 15, 2026 FRUITA, Colo. – Over the past eight years, the North Fruita Desert has changed in ways riders can see as soon as they arrive. There are more miles of singletrack, more places to camp and dedicated space for races and other large events, all part of a broader effort by the Bureau of Land Management and community partners to keep pace with one of western Colorado’s busiest recreation areas. This fall, the final trail in the North Fruita Desert Trails Master Plan is complete. K2-Play winds for about three miles along the base of the Book Cliffs and completes the final phase of a roughly 30-mile expansion of the 18 Road trail system. Its completion caps years of planning and construction involving the BLM Grand Junction Field Office, Colorado Plateau Mountain Bike Trail Association, Mesa County, City of Fruita, local businesses, professional trail builders and volunteers. Phil Westcott From Juneau, to Anchorage, to Nome, and beyond, people in Alaska are often spotted wearing a colorful or patterned hooded garment with a big front pocket. This classic Alaska attire is known as a kuspuk. Kuspuk is an English word based on the Indigenous Yup’ik word “qaspeq” which translates to “cloth over parka.” The original qaspeq was made from gut skin, animal hide, or feathered bird skin to keep the wearer warm and dry—a constant struggle known all too well by those who have live, work, and travel in the arctic. In the 1800s, European whalers brought goods to trade, which included cloth bags filled with flour or sugar. Indigenous (Inupiaq/Yup’ik) women repurposed the cotton flour sacks and sewed a lightweight summer garment that resembled the “over parkas” worn in the winter.Today, kuspuks are often made of colorful or patterned cotton material and are locally hand-made. Kyle Haustveit Kyle Haustveit, Under Secretary of Energy Kyle Haustveit was sworn in as the U.S. Department of Energy's Under Secretary of Energy on May 22, 2026. In this role, Mr. Haustveit provides strategic leadership across several offices dedicated to delivering affordable, reliable, and secure energy to the American people. These include the Offices of Electricity; Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER); Arctic Energy; Indian Energy; Nuclear Energy; Energy Dominance Financing; Hydrocarbons and Geothermal; and the Power Marketing Administrations. Before joining the U.S. Department of Energy, Mr. Haustveit served in a range of technical and leadership roles at Devon Energy. During his tenure, he led teams that developed and commercialized diagnostic techniques now used globally to optimize hydraulic fracturing and resource development. He later directed an Energy Ventures team focused on investments in next-generation energy technologies, including geothermal, carbon utilization, and produced water treatment. La higiene y prevención de virus respiratorios 18 de ago. del 2025 English (US) Lo que debe saber La higiene es un hábito o una práctica regular que mejora la limpieza. Practicar una buena higiene es una estrategia de prevención principal recomendada para todos para disminuir los riesgos de presentar enfermedades respiratorias. Cómo funciona Cubrirse la nariz y la boca al toser y estornudar limita la propagación de microbios para proteger a los demás. Lavarse las manos con jabón elimina los microbios de las manos, lo que hace que sea menos probable que infecten el sistema respiratorio cuando se toca los ojos, la nariz o la boca. Si no hay agua y jabón disponibles, usar un desinfectante de manos con al menos un 60 por ciento de alcohol puede matar estos microbios. The Lakeview District's boundary encompasses approximately 3.5 million acres of public land in Lake, Klamath, and part of Harney counties in south-central and southeastern Oregon. pages.description: The paleontologist who made the discovery was originally at the museum to study a fossil that resembles the Loch Ness monster.
pages.text: Largest 'Sea Dragon' Fossil Accidentally Discovered in Museum | National Geographic 1:00 Artist's impression of the Ichthyosaurus ILLUSTRATION BY JOSCHUA KNÜPPE Largest 'Sea Dragon' Fossil Accidentally Discovered in Museum The paleontologist who made the discovery was originally at the museum to study a fossil that resembles the Loch Ness monster. By Sarah Gibbens Published August 28, 2017 • 4 min read Sven Sachs, a paleontologist from the Bielefeld Natural History Museum in Germany, was at the Lower Saxony State Museum in Hannover to study an ancient sea reptile when one of the museum's display fossils caught his eye. The specimen had originally been unearthed in the mid-1990s in Somerset, England, but it had remained largely unstudied since. Sachs suspected it was an Ichthyosaurus. Commonly mistaken for a dinosaur, the species was more like a "sea dragon" marine reptile that had a long, flexible body and may have swum like eels. "I found it very extraordinary," said Sachs. "[It was] way bigger than any specimen I had examined." He explained the specimen had previously been labeled as a smaller species within the Ichthyosaurus group. Sachs reached out to Ichthyosaurus expert Dean Lomax from the University of Manchester, and in early 2017 they examined the specimen together, finding it to be a specimen of the species Ichthyosaurus somersetensis . Skeleton of Ichthyosaurus . Photograph by Dean Lomax Their findings, published in the journal Acta Palaeontologica Polonica , describe the largest known specimen of its kind. After years writing about music for zines and working in college radio, Gotrich started his career at NPR as an intern for the All Songs Considered podcast in 2006, where he's been a regular presence ever since. He's produced several different series for NPR Music, including First Listen, Song We Love, #NowPlaying and the Listening Party. While Gotrich covers all kinds of music, he is best known as the creator of roséwave, the pop-forward summer music series, and Viking's Choice , a curatorial free-for-all that emphasizes the loud and the weird. Credit: M. King/NIST Even if you’ve never heard of “light caustics,” you’ve probably seen them. They’re the ethereal patterns of light that coat the bottoms of swimming pools and break up the shadows of glass. Anywhere light is bent or reflected by a curved surface, caustics can appear. This trick of the light is turning out to be an important tool for 3D-printing metal, a process in which high-powered lasers melt metal powder one layer at a time. NIST scientists have found that caustic reflections from those lasers contain clues about the metal’s microscopic shape. This research will give us never-before-seen, real-time insights into metal 3D printing. What’s Metal 3D Printing? Intravenous drug delivery methods need to carefully control the flow of medicine into a patient. Knowing the medicine’s flow rate — or the volume of fluid flowing into the patient each second or minute — is crucial to delivering the right amount of medicine at the right time. pages.text: Learn about the United States' founding documents | USAGov Skip to main content Learn about the United States' founding documents The Declaration of Independence, U.S. Constitution, and Bill of Rights, known together as the Charters of Freedom, established the government’s structure and continue to secure the rights of American citizens. Declaration of Independence The Declaration of Independence proclaimed that the American colonies were separating from British rule, and detailed the reasons. On July 4, 1776, Congress voted to accept the Declaration of Independence, marking July 4 as Independence Day. Thomas Jefferson, the principal author, drafted the document in 17 days. U.S. Constitution The Constitution of the United States set up the foundation of the U.S. government, including its purpose and structure. The Constitutional Convention adopted the Constitution on September 17, 1787. Bill of Rights The Bill of Rights is the first 10 amendments (changes) to the U.S. Constitution. It guarantees greater protection for individual freedoms and lists specific limits on government power. The Constitution has 27 amendments in all. Hier soir, j’ai présenté dans l’amphithéâtre C002 au sein du campus de enseeiht à Toulouse, « Contribuez à OSM ». La bonne surprise fut le taux de remplissage de la salle. J’ai compté plus d’une vingtaine de personnes.
